analysis.evidence: אֱלֹהִים is the subject, אֹתָם refers to the lights as the direct object, and בִּרְקִיעַ הַשָּׁמָיִם specifies where God set them.
analysis.morphology: Qal wayyiqtol, third person masculine singular, with prefixed וַ־ and no suffix
analysis.sense: put or set something in a place

analysis.evidence: אֱלֹהִים is the subject of וַיִּתֵּן, “he set.” The masculine singular verb identifies God as the one who set the lights in the expanse of the heavens.
analysis.morphology: Masculine plural common noun in the absolute state, with singular verb agreement.

analysis.evidence: The construct noun takes הַשָּׁמָיִם as its complement. The phrase בִּרְקִיעַ הַשָּׁמָיִם identifies where God placed the lights: “in the expanse of the heavens.”
analysis.morphology: Masculine singular construct noun with prefixed preposition בִּ, “in.”

analysis.evidence: In בִּרְקִיעַ הַשָּׁמָיִם, “in the expanse of the sky,” the noun identifies the sky as the place where God set the lights to shine on the earth.
analysis.morphology: Definite article הַ־ + masculine plural common noun in the absolute state.

analysis.evidence: God sets the luminaries in the expanse of the heavens. לְהָאִיר gives the purpose of their placement, and עַל הָאָרֶץ specifies where they give light.
analysis.morphology: Hiphil infinitive construct with prefixed לְ expressing purpose

analysis.evidence: In לְהָאִיר עַל הָאָרֶץ, “to shine upon the earth,” עַל introduces הָאָרֶץ as the surface on which the light falls.
God places the lights בִּרְקִיעַ הַשָּׁמָיִם, “in the expanse of the heavens,” לְהָאִיר עַל הָאָרֶץ, “to shine on the earth.” The pairing of heavens and earth identifies the earth as a whole.
analysis.morphology: Common noun, singular absolute, of common gender, with prefixed definite article הָ־.
